content: The diagnosis of post-bariatric surgery hypoglycemia (PBSH) requires a thorough evaluation of the patient’s medical history, dietary habits, and activity patterns. It is also essential to rule out other potential causes of hypoglycemia, such as malnutrition, adverse effects of medications, dumping syndrome, or insulinoma. The initial approach to managing PBSH involves dietary modifications. Patients are advised to consume slower-absorbing carbohydrates, along with adequate protein and healthy fats, to help stabilize blood glucose levels and prevent rapid drops in glucose. Nutritional therapy provided by dietitians who have expertise in managing PBSH is strongly recommended. Additionally, the use of real-time continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) can be particularly beneficial, especially for individuals who experience hypoglycemia unawareness. In cases where dietary adjustments alone are insufficient, medications may be considered. Acarbose can be prescribed to slow the absorption of carbohydrates, while diazoxide and octreotide may be used to reduce the secretion of glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) and insulin. These pharmacological interventions aim to better regulate glucose levels and mitigate hypoglycemic episodes.
